legend: Sagittal CT (A), T2-weighted MRI (B), and contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted MRI (C) sequences show a peripheral chondrosarcoma arising from the superior pubic ramus in a patient with hereditary multiple osteochondromas. The cartilage cap was 70 mm thick. Septonodular contrast enhancement seen is typical of cartilaginous tumours, and extensive non-enhancing areas are in keeping with myxoid components.
A high-grade chondrosarcoma arising in an osteochondroma of the sacrum. The cartilaginous cap is thick (maximum thickness: 70 mm), lobulated, and shows myxoid change.
Grade 2 chondrosarcoma arising in a solitary osteochondroma of the pelvis. The cartilaginous cap is thick and nodular.
A higher-power view of the tumour in the pelvis that arises from an osteochondroma shows increased cellularity, nuclear atypia, and a permeative growth pattern with entrapment of trabecular bone.
